PullRequest.Title: sessions: run Agent Merge per chat folder and present multi-folder sessions
PullRequest.Body:
Continues chat-folder separation in the Agents Window: chats in one session can work in different folders, and everything a chat shows or does is scoped to its own folders.

## Agent Merge per folder

Agent Merge now runs separately for each folder a chat works in, instead of once per session.

- **Host:** runs Agent Merge separately for each folder, each with its own settings, bound pull request, feedback watermark and repair budget. Repair turns and notices go to the chat that turned Agent Merge on (else the first chat in that folder; the default chat for the session folder). Repairs run concurrently per chat, and elevated approvals stay applied while any folder runs. Settings from earlier versions are read as the session folder's and migrated on first write.
- **Client:** Agent Merge actions, context keys and the chat input's pull request pill follow the folder the active chat works in. Session-wide surfaces (sessions list, blocked sessions) keep the session folder, matching the pull request they show.
- **Hardening (from reviews):**
  - **Client writes:** a client writes only the folder it changes, by working directory. The host merges the write into the other folders and derives the key itself, so a stale client copy can't undo host changes, and keys match across platforms. The host drops entries for folders or chats outside the session.
  - **Host writes:** lifecycle writes re-read current state and write only host-owned state. A config replacement no longer overwrites Agent Merge settings.
  - **Tool authorization:** Agent Merge tools act for the invoking chat, and only the chat running a repair turn can use its authorization.
  - **Lifecycle:** turning a folder off, or creating a pull request with Agent Merge, starts fresh. A folder no chat works in any more turns Agent Merge off with a reason. Removing a chat ends its repair turn and moves its pending notices to the default chat.

## Multi-folder presentation and restore

- **Restore:** the host persists the latest Git state for each chat's working-directory scope, so chats in other folders show their own branch state right after a restore.
- **Session hover:** in a multi-folder session, it summarizes every workspace, its changes and pull requests. A chat's hover shows its own folder, branch changes and pull requests, and the sessions list shows chat rows accordingly.
- **Changes view and banners:** the Changes view hides Session Changes in multi-folder sessions, and the input banners follow the active chat's folder.

## Notes for reviewers

- Mixed client and host versions are not handled for the new per-folder Agent Merge settings. An older remote host ignores them, and an older client stops seeing Agent Merge once the host migrates the old format.
- Follow-ups:
  - Session creation still copies Agent Merge keys from the client request. The old host-owned key was already copied before this change.
  - Folders that differ only in path case on a Linux host collide on the client.

## Validation

- Typecheck, eslint and hygiene are clean.
- 7,816 Agent Host tests, 4,499 sessions tests and 1,714 workbench agent-session tests pass.
- New tests cover per-folder reads and writes, host-side merging, tool authorization per chat, chat removal, lifecycle resets, and folders without chats.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed cache shape, insertion path, chat-removal lifecycle, and whole-session-only cleanup are directly visible. Exact memory per chat is small and workload-dependent, which is why severity is low, but retention and linear growth with chat churn are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-chat observable graphs, configuration-event wrappers, provider observables, and chat URI keys
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained objects grow linearly with the number of distinct chats that have been active during a session, including chats later removed; the outer WeakMap is collectible only when the entire session is released.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Long-lived multi-chat sessions accumulate retained objects and eventually incur higher memory and GC pressure as chats/subagent chats churn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The cache held one Agent Merge state observable and one configuration observable per session, so chat creation/removal did not increase retained cache entries.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new nested Maps cache a separate state/configuration observable for each chat URI, while neither this helper nor the provider's matching `_agentMergeSessionStateObservables` Map removes a key when that chat disappears; cleanup is only performed when the whole session is removed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `WeakMap<ISession, Map<string, ...>>` declarations at lines 19-20 replace the previous single observable per session with history-keyed per-chat Maps; added `byChat.set(chatCacheKey(...))` then retains each distinct chat entry.
Findings.Title: Evict Agent Merge observables when chats are removed
Findings.Impact: Opening Agent Merge UI surfaces for a sequence of peer or tool-created chats and then removing those chats leaves one client state observable, one derived configuration observable (including its global configuration event wrapper), and one provider observable cached per historical chat until the session itself is discarded.
Findings.Evidence: `setCached` inserts every non-main chat under `chat.resource.toString()` into both nested Maps. There is no deletion path in this module. The provider similarly stores each chat in `_agentMergeSessionStateObservables` at `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:4769`, and only deletes the entire per-session map in `_removeCachedSession` at line 6997; chat metadata removal updates the live chat collection without pruning these caches.
Findings.Recommendation: Tie both cache layers to chat lifecycle: use a weak cache keyed by the live `IChat` object where possible, and prune provider URI entries whenever the session's chat metadata removes a chat (retaining only the `''` session-folder entry and currently live chat URIs).

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or enable Agent Merge for several chat folders in one session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each enabled folder schedules its own evaluation; branch/target resolution, pull-request association, and the first authoritative pull-request refresh must complete before that folder can evaluate blockers or start a repair. Other folders progress independently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Git state/current branch and, around repair turns, repository root and HEAD
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one recovery Git-state refresh per cold folder runtime when branch data is missing; local commit reads occur per repair/merge evaluation that requires a baseline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Merge performed this work only for the session folder; the PR extends it to each enabled distinct folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Branch resolution blocks binding/evaluation for that folder; local commit resolution blocks starting or completing the relevant repair transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve credentials, associate the folder branch with a pull request, subscribe, and authoritatively refresh PR fragments
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold subscription/refresh per distinct enabled folder/PR; warm cycles reuse resources. Requests are bounded by the shared GitHub request queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Agent Merge runtime could monitor the session-folder PR; the PR allows one per enabled folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first authoritative snapshot is required before blocker evaluation for that folder.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start an Agent Merge repair turn in the owning chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active repair turn per enabled folder runtime/chat, bounded by persisted repair budgets; distinct chats may run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repair ownership and concurrency were session/default-chat scoped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repair completion is the work itself; it does not block unrelated folder runtimes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the number of distinct enabled folder keys after folder deduplication, not the number of chats; chats sharing a folder share one runtime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Evaluations are serialized per runtime key but run across folder keys. GitHub requests then pass through the shared request queue, capped at four globally and two per host/account constraints; repair turns can run concurrently in distinct chats by design.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold folders create a pull-request subscription and authoritatively load requested fragments. Warm evaluations reuse the subscription and snapshot, with event debounce and a ten-minute backstop; pull-request resources coalesce subscriptions for the same normalized ref.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: per-folder runtime keys and independent sequencers are explicit, and transport-level request limits/coalescing were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions with many simultaneously enabled Agent Merge folders may be uncommon; aggregate agent-turn cost depends on provider behavior. Network concurrency is concretely bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the fan-out implements the requested per-folder behavior, expensive network work is globally bounded/coalesced, and independent repair concurrency is intentional; no separate concrete degradation was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh and restore folder-scoped Git and Branch Changes state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A chat Git refresh computes Git state and now persists changed peer-folder state before firing its refresh event; branch changes publish before fire-and-forget cache writes. Restore-time scoped Branch Changes reads are asynchronous and do not block registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read repository Git state and compute branch diffs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One throttled Git-state operation per interested source; one debounced branch diff per distinct subscribed scope after grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These Git operations already ran; the PR changes peer-folder persistence and restoration, not the core Git/diff boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Git-state computation precedes state publication; branch diff computation precedes changeset publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the complete folder-scope Git-state map when a peer chat's Git state changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized metadata write per actual changed peer-folder Git state, after the five-second refresh throttle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat Git state was held only in memory and caused no database write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the refresh event, but the payload is one compact Git-state record per known scope.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the scoped Branch Changes metadata blob
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per distinct owner on cold registration and one asynchronous write per successful branch recompute; session-folder recomputes additionally retain the legacy writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session-folder branch cache used existing metadata keys and peer-folder branch caches were not persisted in the containing session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restore read is asynchronous after changeset registration; persistence writes occur after publication and are not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct normalized workspace scopes and changed files in each branch diff. Git refreshes are throttled per source to at most one cycle per five seconds; changeset recomputation is debounced and folder scopes are deduplicated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Git refreshes serialize per session/chat key. Git-data database saves serialize per containing session. Scoped Branch Changes restores are one pending task per owner; metadata writes are asynchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restore reads one scoped metadata key per distinct owner and seeds only an empty changeset. Warm operation reuses restored/live state. Git-data writes replace the containing session's current scope map; missing/unavailable state removes the relevant scope.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call paths, sequencing, debounce, and awaited versus fire-and-forget placement are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large changed-file lists increase serialization and write bytes, but the added scoped write is off the publication critical path and recomputation remains debounced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: additional persistence is bounded by real state changes/debounced recomputes and largely off the critical path; evidence did not establish a material latency or throughput regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch among and remove chats while Agent Merge UI surfaces observe folder state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active-chat toolbar, context keys, and banners synchronously obtain cached per-chat observables; no external boundary must complete for presentation once session state is present.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct chat URIs ever activated during the lifetime of one retained session, including removed peer and tool-created chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are event-driven; old observables generally lose active subscribers when UI surfaces switch chats, but their objects remain cached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm lookups reuse per-chat entries. There is no eviction or invalidation on chat removal in either the session helper's nested Maps or the provider's per-session nested Map; only whole-session removal clears the provider map, and the WeakMap releases its nested maps only when the session object is collected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: insertion and cleanup paths were directly traced, including whole-session-only provider cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-entry retained size is modest, and the impact depends on chat churn and session lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: the new history-keyed per-chat observable caches grow without a chat-lifecycle eviction path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render session/chat rows and open multi-folder summary hovers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row rendering computes folder labels/icons and installs delayed hover factories. Aggregate workspace/change/PR scanning and DOM construction occur only when the hover content is requested.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible chats, workspace folders, and deduplicated pull-request refs across session/chat workspaces.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work is confined to row autoruns and hover construction; no added asynchronous fan-out was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rows are virtualized and template disposables are cleared on reuse. Hover content reads current observables; PR refs are deduplicated by URI in a temporary Map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: render and delayed-hover call paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions with very many chats/folders make hover construction linear, but realistic cardinality is modest and work is deferred until hover.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added aggregate scans are deferred, linear in visible session metadata, and do not cross filesystem/network/IPC boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all changed files. One low-severity unbounded-retention issue was reported for per-chat Agent Merge observable caches. Per-folder Agent Merge boundary fan-out, Git/changeset persistence, and multi-folder presentation were traced with their cache, critical-path, and concurrency behavior; no other high-confidence regression met the reporting threshold.
